title: Local Power of Causal Stochastic Dominance Tests under Rough Nuisance Functions
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field; paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4; mathematics passes, no bounded in-scope field lift.
gap_reasons: Theorem 3 delivers an n-first two-sided excess-power bracket establishing positivity and faster-than-polynomial decay, but leaves logarithmic scales c^{-1/2} and c^{-4} far apart.

The converse uses an X-independent randomized submodel and adapts the established [orthant moment-prior mechanism](https://arxiv.org/html/1702.03760), so it does not isolate a deterioration attributable to critical confounding.

The constructive family establishes full-class attainability, but its exponential cap supplies an existence benchmark without demonstrated feasible computation or practically informative power guarantees.
proof_attempt_summary: Derived and reviewed an original-record exact-size attaining family and a legal growing-atom converse for critical causal dominance. The repaired signed-prior construction and three primary-source attestations pass the current math and rubric panels, but the final general review grades incremental below field (6.4 < 7.4), with no bounded in-scope improvement. The c^{-1/2} versus c^{-4} logarithmic-rate gap remains open; no Lean formalization was launched, and result-level citation placement plus the continuity locator pagination remain presentation caveats.
tldr: Causal dominance compares intervention distributions through the positive part of their CDF contrast. For the publicly known uniform design and unknown nuisance functions with H\"older exponent \(1/4\), the paper proves \(e^{-C_1/c^4}\le b_-(c)-\alpha\le b_+(c)-\alpha\le C_0e^{-\kappa/\sqrt c}\), with \(\alpha=1/10\). A total observable randomized family gives the lower inequality with exact finite-sample size control; normalized legal priors with individually separated alternatives and increasing outcome-atom complexity give the upper inequality. The excess power is positive at every fixed \(c\) and decreases faster than every polynomial as \(c\downarrow0\). The calibration, rational evaluator and prior transfer are proved. The acknowledged remaining question is whether the two logarithmic scales can be matched or normalized to a limit.
gap: Regular causal-CDF inference and scalar higher-order rate results do not by themselves quantify all-test small-signal power on the specified full critical class. Gaussian orthant priors supply a method, but not the required observable calibration or causal original-record transfer.
fill: Theorem 3 combines an exact-size constructive lower gain with a growing-outcome all-test converse. Open-ended Question 1 isolates the uniform expectation certificate, numerical enclosures and total evaluator needed by the constructive theorem.
